key_insight: AEAPTMS passivation makes perovskite surface electrostatics more uniform and light-stable, indicating fewer grain-boundary barriers and less electronic disorder.
engineering_relevance: This suggests amino-silane surface treatment can improve perovskite solar-cell voltage loss mitigation by stabilizing carrier landscapes at the nanoscale.
method: Compare dark CPD and illuminated SPV before vs after AEAPTMS passivation
Separate grain-boundary and grain-interior surface-potential contributions
evidence_signal: Passivation narrowed dark CPD spread from about 45.7 to 14.6 mV, increased steady-state SPV from about 345 to 417 mV, and reduced SPV stabilization time from about 840 to 470 s.
watch_item: These conclusions come from thin-film nanoscale measurements, so device-level performance gains and long-term operational stability still need direct validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
